'''100,000''' ('''one hundred thousand''') is the [[natural number]] following [[90,000#Selected numbers in the range 90,000–99,999|99,999]] and preceding 100,001. In scientific notation, it is written as 10<sup>5</sup>.

== Terms for 100,000 ==
In [[Bangladesh]], [[India]], [[Pakistan]] and [[South Asia]], one hundred thousand is called a [[lakh]], and is written as '''1,00,000'''.<ref name=EB1911>{{cite EB1911 |wstitle=Lakh |volume=16 |page=94}}</ref> The [[Thai language|Thai]], [[Lao language|Lao]], [[Khmer language|Khmer]] and [[Vietnamese language|Vietnamese]] languages also have separate words for this number: {{lang|th|แสน}}, {{lang|lo|ແສນ}}, {{lang|km|សែន}} (all ''saen''), and {{lang|vi|ức}} respectively. The [[Malagasy language|Malagasy]] word is {{lang|mg|hetsy}}.<ref>{{Cite web |date=26 October 2017 |title=Malagasy Dictionary and Madagascar Encyclopedia : hetsy |url=http://malagasyword.org/bins/teny2/hetsy |access-date=31 December 2019 |website=malagasyword.org}}</ref>

In [[Netherlands|the Netherlands]], a '[[:nl:Ton_(geld)|ton]]' is a colloquialism for a denomination of 100.000 monetary units. In the [[Dutch guilder|guilders]] period a ton would denote 100.000 guilders. With the introduction of the euro, a ton would come to mean 100.000 euros. Usage is mostly limited to the financial sphere and to the buying and selling of houses. It is not used in official settings because of the ambiguity with the commonly used [[Tonne|metric tonne]]. While usage is common in the Netherlands, it sees almost no use in [[Belgium]].{{cn|date=July 2024}}

In [[Cyrillic numerals]], it is known as the legion ({{script|Cyrl|легион}}): [[File:Legion-1000000-Cyrillic.svg|30px]] or [[File:Несведь.svg|25px]].

== Values of 100,000 ==
In [[astronomy]], '''100,000 metres''', '''100 kilometres''', or '''100&nbsp;km''' (62 miles) is the [[altitude]] at which the [[Fédération Aéronautique Internationale]] (FAI) defines [[spaceflight]] to begin.

In [[paleoclimatology]], the [[100,000-year problem]] is a mismatch between the temperature record and the modeled [[solar irradiation|incoming solar radiation]].

In the [[Irish language]], '''{{wikt-lang|ga|céad míle fáilte|céad míle fáilte}}''' ({{IPA|ga|ˌceːd̪ˠ ˈmʲiːlʲə ˈfˠaːl̠ʲtʲə|pron}}) is a popular greeting meaning "a hundred thousand welcomes".

* '''694,280''' = Keith number<ref name=A007629/>

{{redirect|999999|the string of nines in pi|Six nines in pi}}
* '''900,001''' = prime number
* '''901,971''' = number of free 14-ominoes
* '''909,091''' = [[unique prime]] in base 10

* '''925,765''' = [[Markov number]]<ref name=A002559/>
* '''925,993''' = Keith number<ref name=A007629/>

The reciprocal of this number, in its expanded form, lists all three-digit numbers in order except 998.<ref>{{cite web |date=23 January 2012 |title=Dividing one by 998001 produces list of three digit numbers |url=https://www.themarysue.com/one-divided-by-998001/}}</ref>
* '''998,991''' = largest [[triangular number]] with 6 digits and the 1413th triangular number
* '''999,983''' = largest 6-digit prime number and largest 6-digit [[palindromic prime]]<ref>{{Cite OEIS|A007500|Primes whose reversal in base 10 is also prime (called "palindromic primes" by David Wells, although that name usually refers to A002385). Also called reversible primes.}}</ref>
* '''999,999''' = repdigit. [[Rational number]]s with denominators 7 and 13 have 6-digit [[repetend]]s when expressed in [[decimal]] form, because 999999 is the smallest number one less than a power of 10 that is divisible by 7 and by 13.

===Prime numbers===

There are '''9,592''' primes less than 10<sup>5</sup>, where 99,991 is the largest prime number smaller than 100,000.

Increments of 10<sup>5</sup> from 100,000 through a [[1,000,000|one million]] have the following prime counts:

*'''8,392''' primes between 100,000 and 200,000.{{efn|content=Smallest ''p'' > 100,000 is 100,003 (9,593rd); largest ''p'' < 200,000 is 199,999 (17,984th).}} This is a difference of [[1200 (number)|1,200]] primes from the previous range.
**104,729 is the 10,000th prime, which is in this range.
**199,999 is prime.
*'''8,013''' primes between 200,000 and 300,000.{{efn|content=Smallest ''p'' > 200,000 is 200,003 (17,985th); largest ''p'' < 300,000 is 299,993 (25,997th).}} A difference of [[379 (number)|379]] primes from the previous range.
**224,737 is the 20,000th prime.
*'''7,863''' primes between 300,000 and 400,000.{{efn|content=Smallest ''p'' > 300,000 is 300,007 (25,998th); largest ''p'' < 400,000 is 399,989 (33,860th).}} A difference of [[150 (number)|150]] primes from the previous range.
** 350,377 is the 30,000th prime.
*'''7,678''' primes between 400,000 and 500,000.{{efn|content=Smallest ''p'' > 400,000 is 400,009 (33,861st); largest ''p'' < 500,000 is 499,979 (41,538th).}} A difference of [[185 (number)|185]] primes from the previous range. Here, the difference increases by a count of [[35 (number)|35]].
** 479,909 is the 40,000th prime.
* '''7,560''' primes between 500,000 and 600,000.{{efn|content=Smallest ''p'' > 500,000 is 500,009 (41,539th); largest ''p'' < 600,000 is 599,999 (49,098th).}} A difference of [[118 (number)|118]] primes from the previous range.
**'''[[7560 (number)|7,560]]''' is the twentieth highly composite number.<ref name=A002182/>
**599,999 is prime.
*'''7,445''' primes between 600,000 and 700,000.{{efn|content=Smallest ''p'' > 600,000 is 600,011 (49,099th); largest ''p'' < 700,000 is 699,967 (56,543rd).}} A difference of [[115 (number)|115]] primes from the previous range.
** 611,953 is the 50,000th prime.
*'''7,408''' primes between 700,000 and 800,000.{{efn|content=Smallest ''p'' > 700,000 is 700,001 (56,544th); largest ''p'' < 800,000 is 799,999 (63,951st).}} A difference of [[37 (number)|37]] primes from the previous range.
**700,001 and 799,999 are both prime. 
**746,773 is the 60,000th prime.
*'''7,323''' primes between 800,000 and 900,000.{{efn|content=Smallest ''p'' > 800,000 is 800,011 (63,952nd); largest ''p'' < 900,000 is 899,981 (71,274th).}} A difference of [[85 (number)|85]] primes from the previous range. Here, the difference increases by a count of [[48 (number)|48]]. 
** 882,377 is the 70,000th prime.
*'''7,224''' primes between 900,000 and [[1,000,000]].{{efn|content=Smallest ''p'' > 900,000 is 900,001 (71,275th); largest ''p'' < [[1,000,000]] is 999,983 (78,498th).}} A difference of [[99 (number)|99]] primes from the previous range. The difference increases again, by a count of [[14 (number)|14]].
** 900,001 is prime.
In total, there are '''68,906''' prime numbers between 100,000 and 1,000,000.<ref>{{Cite web |last1=Caldwell |first1=Chris K. |author-link=PrimePages |title=The Nth Prime Page |url=https://primes.utm.edu/nthprime/ |access-date=3 December 2022 |website=PrimePages}} From the differences of the [[Sequence|prime indexes]] of the smallest and largest prime numbers in ranges of increments of 10<sup>5</sup></ref>
